text:
maria (AE): Hey team — FinTrust just confirmed they need a POC in an isolated network (no egress). Asking for packaging options, expected upgrade cadence, and any runtime constraints. They also want a short checklist we can hand to their infra team.

sam (Solutions Eng): OK. quick clarifying Qs: do they need UI/console access inside the isolated env or is a fully headless inference-only bundle fine? Also do they want offline activation (license key) or an operator will toggle entitlements locally?

maria (AE): Headless inference only to start. Operator will manage licenses; they prefer no outbound activation.

sam (Solutions Eng): Got it. We have two delivery formats: 1) containerized offline bundle (tar with images + signed manifests + installer script) and 2) VM appliance (OVF) for air-gapped datacenters. For fully offline activation we can emit a signed license file they drop into /etc/redwood/license.json. No outbound calls required.

devon (Platform Eng): A few engineering notes:
- offline bundle size: ~12GB for trimmed runtime + model shard metadata (varies by model).
- fast path: customers can use quantized model variants to reduce size to ~4–6GB.
- delta upgrades: we support binary delta patches for the runtime and model diffs. We recommend nominal cadence: security patches ASAP, minor patches monthly, model weight updates quarterly unless customer requests more frequent.

lee (Security): From the questionnaire side: we can provide SBOM, signed artifacts (Ed25519), and FIPS-compliant crypto support if they require it. For KMS/HSM: offline mode accepts locally mounted HSM or PKCS#11-compatible devices.

maria (AE): Helpful. FinTrust asked about upgrade windows — they have change-control windows once per quarter. That means we need a painless delta approach. Is rollback supported?

devon (Platform Eng): Yes. We produce reversible deltas and keep three previous versions by default to allow quick rollback. For strict change-control windows we can schedule rollouts as staged jobs: canary on a single node, verify health, then roll through cluster. All steps are orchestrated by the local operator; the installer exposes a dry-run flag. Example: `./install.sh --dry-run --target /opt/redwood`

sam (Solutions Eng): Also note we can provide a pre-packed compatibility checklist for their infra team. Items include: minimum kernel (4.19+), required kernel modules (overlay, br_netfilter), required ports (none required outbound; inbound ports: 8080 for API, 8443 for console if console included), minimum RAM/GPU per model profile, available disk space. I can draft that.

lee (Security): Add to the checklist: verified artifact checksum verification step. We provide both SHA256 and Ed25519 signatures. Example verification snippet for operators:

```
# verify sha256
sha256sum -c redwood-runtime.tar.gz.sha256
# verify signature
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify vendor_pubkey.pem -signature redwood-runtime.tar.gz.sig redwood-runtime.tar.gz
```

maria (AE): Perfect. They also asked about embedded telemetry — they insist on zero telemetry. Can we ship with all telemetry disabled by default?

devon (Platform Eng): Yes. Offline bundle defaults to telemetry=off. The config file `config.yaml` toggles telemetry and sets network_policy: "isolated". We also ship an example systemd unit and an offline healthcheck tool.

sam (Solutions Eng): For licensing: operator-driven activation means they upload the license file and run `redwoodctl license apply /path/to/license.json`. The license is signed and contains allowed models + expiry. No phone-home required.

deploy-bot: Build artifact ready: redwood-offline-bundle-2026.11.03-rc2 (sha256: 3a7f...e9c)

maria (AE): Timeline ask from FinTrust: demo inside their isolated lab next Tuesday (needs docs + checklist by Friday). Can we commit to a checklist + signed bundle by Friday EOD?

sam (Solutions Eng): I'll own the checklist + packaging. devon — can you confirm the RC2 bundle can be promoted and we can generate a signed license sample for them by Friday?

devon (Platform Eng): I can do the promotion and sign a sample license. Two caveats: we need confirmation on which model family they want (base large vs. quantized) so we can include the appropriate shard set. If they want a GPU runtime, we need to know the node GPU type (A10G vs A100) for optimal kernel selection.

maria (AE): I'll get that from FinTrust today. Also they asked about offline security questionnaire items: do we have canned answers for "does product phone home" and "what data is collected"?

lee (Security): Yes — canned answers: "Product does not phone home in offline mode. No customer content is transmitted. Only optional operator-provided telemetry is possible and disabled by default." I can paste the standard Q responses into the checklist doc.

maria (AE): Awesome. One last: legal wants to know upgrade cadence variability for SLAs. Can we promise quarterly model updates and emergency security patches within 72 hours?

sam (Solutions Eng): Typical commitment: quarterly model updates included in POC/entitlements; emergency security patches we commit to make available as a signed offline patch within 72 hours of severity confirmation. We can include that language in the SOW.

maria (AE): Great — thanks. Action items: sam to draft checklist + deliver Friday, devon to promote bundle and produce sample license, lee to paste questionnaire answers into checklist. I'll confirm model selection & GPU type with FinTrust today. :thumbsup:

sam (Solutions Eng): ack. I'll create the checklist doc and link it here when ready.

deploy-bot: Signed bundle uploaded to internal artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood.local/offline/redwood-offline-bundle-2026.11.03-rc2.tar.gz.sig

maria (AE): Thanks all.
